title: TrendAI: BYOD extortion group claims hospitals and universities, ransom audio played at UNM
date_note: Date is TrendAI's publication of its report; the incidents it describes ran from 5 October to 9 November 2026.
org: BYOD ransomware group (University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center, Vanderbilt University, Michigan State University)
geo_basis: Victims named in the report are US institutions; pinned at the country, not one victim
summary: TrendAI says a ransomware and extortion group calling itself BYOD, first seen in September 2026, has claimed at least nine organisations between 5 October and 9 November. At UNM Health Sciences Center, ambulances were diverted and more than 30 clinics cancelled appointments and outpatient surgeries; UNM says core systems were not penetrated. Vanderbilt has not confirmed BYOD's involvement, encryption or data theft. BYOD's larger claims are unverified.
plain: A group calling itself BYOD says it has hit hospitals and universities. UNM's hospital diverted ambulances for a time. The group's larger claims have not been confirmed by the victims.
exec: A new extortion group has disrupted US health and education bodies; its claims exceed what victims confirm.
action: Follow TrendAI's advice: review privileged accounts, use phishing-resistant MFA, keep tested offline backups, and review what a compromised account accessed before its reset.
impact: UNM Health Sciences Center: ambulances diverted 12:30 to 2:30 p.m. on 26 October; more than 30 clinics cancelled appointments and outpatient surgeries.

validation.note: TrendAI's own report and Cyber Security News both state the campaign, the UNM disruption and that the group's larger claims are unverified. Group figures (36,000 systems, 1.3 million MSU students, over one million SSNs at Vanderbilt) are BYOD's claims only.

review.note: TrendAI 18 Nov and Cyber Security News checked: nine orgs 5 Oct to 9 Nov, UNM 26 Oct diversion, 30+ clinics, Vanderbilt unconfirmed, claims unverified all match. Action listed alerts on MFA bursts and bulk exports not found in pages read; replaced with advice confirmed in the sources.
